contradictions.fact: round-trip distance and gain figures disagree

claims.says: 3.5 (one-way)

rated Hard at 7.0 miles round trip with 3,500 ft of gain to a 6,129-ft high point; it is elsewhere described as closer to two miles one way with 3,700 ft of gain, or roughly 4,000 ft. The discrepancy is real...
distMi: 5.3, gainFt: 3911 (notes: 'Distance and gain are round trip to the true summit')

contradictions.why: 2x the waypoint one-way distance (3.5 mi) gives 7.0 mi round trip, matching beta's first citation, but approach_variants explicitly labels 5.3 mi as the round-trip figure - a 32% gap. Gain also spans 3,500 / 3,700-4,000 / 3,911 / 3,847 for the same climb.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The route's own beta text acknowledges the mileage discrepancy exists and attributes it to different start points/how much of the logging road is counted, but doesn't resolve which number the header should show; the waypoint-implied 7.0 mi round trip is corroborated by beta's own citation, making approach_variants' 5.3 mi the more likely outlier.

contradictions.fact: climb length (length_m) appears to include the non-technical approach

claims.says: Step 1 (Lower) 300 ft, Step 2 (Crux) 400 ft, Step 3 220 ft, Step 4 (Upper) 250 ft — sums to 1,170 ft (~357 m)
...the lower approach involves fighting through approximately 2,300 vertical feet of dense brush...before any technical rock climbing begins...

contradictions.why: length_m (rendered as 'climb length' in TECHNICAL STATS) is over 3x the sum of the route's own four named technical steps (1,170 ft); the gap (~2,330 ft) closely matches the route's own stated 2,300 ft of non-technical brush approach, suggesting length_m was computed by folding the approach into the climb length.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The four named steps (300+400+220+250=1,170 ft) are corroborated by the waypoint directions text verbatim; length_m is the likely outlier, inflated by the approach distance.

contradictions.fact: trailhead waypoint coordinates are geometrically impossible for this route

claims.says: 47.776833, -121.344633 (same value repeated)
one-way distance is about 2.4 miles (4.8 mi round trip)

contradictions.why: The straight-line distance between the trailhead's own coordinates and the summit's own coordinates on this route is roughly 3.6-3.7 miles - farther than the route's own stated 2.4-mile one-way trail distance, which is impossible (a trail can't be shorter than the straight line between its endpoints). All other waypoints on this route cluster correctly near the real peak; only the trailhead coordinate (and its duplicate in approach_logistics) is out of place.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The trailhead elevation (3,480 ft) matches the route's own approach text, so only the lat/lng pair looks wrong/contaminated, not the whole waypoint.
